headline: GIA and Gübelin Gem Lab Confirm Ethiopia as a New Source of Paraíba Tourmaline
short_headline: GIA & Gübelin Confirm Ethiopian Paraíba Tourmaline
summary: GIA and the Gübelin Gem Lab independently confirmed that Ethiopia is a new source of copper-bearing tourmaline that meets the widely accepted definition of Paraíba tourmaline. Gübelin assembled approximately 300 rough and faceted reference stones, while GIA examined a parcel of more than 100 samples. GIA states that it can now confidently identify Ethiopia as an origin on Tourmaline Identification and Origin Reports. This does not mean every Ethiopian tourmaline is Paraíba; individual stones still require proper gemological testing and must meet accepted Paraíba criteria.
key_points: Independent confirmation by GIA and Gübelin Gem Lab
Ethiopia recognized as a new source of Paraíba tourmaline
GIA detailed study: more than 100 samples
GIA can now identify Ethiopia as origin on Tourmaline Identification and Origin Reports
Not every Ethiopian tourmaline is Paraíba; laboratory verification remains essential
source_name: GIA / Gübelin Gem Lab joint announcement

publish_policy.editorial_note: Use the official confirmation as the lead. Do not imply that all Ethiopian tourmaline qualifies as Paraíba.

market_view: GIA and Gübelin's confirmation expands the documented geographic origins of copper-bearing Paraíba tourmaline. Origin claims for individual stones still require laboratory analysis; the announcement alone does not establish their identity or value.
